questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I was just going to mark mulltiple. academic opportunities, language, friends, cultural learning.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: level of the university and the courses offered

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy-ish, the communication between institutions was very poor, which resulted in recieving info about our introduction on 3 different e-mails, but as soon as we where there, all was good, and the overview was accessible.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: none. other than the questions we asked, and the e-mails provided.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: most people find it exceedingly difficult, we however were lucky, and got the first place we applied to. SSH

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: do it, 90% of your time will be spent of campus, so might as well live in the city where you can explore.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: the place we had was terrible

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: communication was very poor.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: we had to find our own courses through osiris, which was very difficult, since the course overview is very confusing, and the time table format is difficult to understand. then we had to do an application for every potential course we wanted to attend, some with extra information needed, like proof of completed courses and abilities. then we where informed about which courses we had been accepted too, which in our cases was all of them, so we had to un-enroll from some of them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: e-mails, we didn't get any help, we were just sent the emails with details on what they needed

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: fully.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do it immediately, so you don't end up stressed by the slow pace of the bureaucratic part of large institutions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: very varying, some very easy, some very motivating. all on level 3.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: it differed from course to course, i would say it is similar. though UCPH seems more standardized

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Criminal behavior during the life-course, theoretical construction and statistical modeling, self-regulation, and science of happiness

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: self regulation and science of happiness, interesting reading, stimulating. Extremely interesting and interdisciplinary. plus unstressful exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many they can't be listed, both sports, art, debate and more, personally i was part of the rugby society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: rugby, amazing sport, amazing people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: experience the city, and amsterdam, visit other cities like breda or gronningen, really cozy, though transport is expensive

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, denmark and the the netherlands is very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: initiate, most people are dutch, so if you don't initiate, they won't

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, except for maybe the language, they fall into dutch quickly, so its easy to feel left out. everyone speaks english though, so not a big problem

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: the layout of the cities and the language, oeh and some good bitterballen

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: make sure to have enough money. make sure to study, it is more difficult to pass some courses, even though the courses might be a bit easier. make sure to go out and explore, that's why you are here.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not really, maybe that grades are weird, 5.5-8 is kind of the same as 4-12, meaning that everything over and 8 is really good, and 02 isn't passing

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: difficult to pinpoint, the whole thing was enjoyable

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: money

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
